analysis.title: Tarsus Pharmaceuticals (TARS): XDEMVY's Charitable Foundation Scheme, Specialty Pharmacy Gimmicks, and Make-Believe TAM
key_insights: Culper is short TARS. Its thesis is that XDEMVY growth has relied on a company-funded charitable foundation Medicare copay scheme (Healthwell Foundation blepharitis fund) that raises Anti-Kickback Statute concerns and could draw a Department of Justice action.

Healthwell launched its blepharitis fund in September 2023, one month after the August 2023 XDEMVY launch. Culper estimates Tarsus donations of $5.7M in 2023, $31.2M in 2024 and $78.5M in 2025, derived from deferred tax assets on charitable contributions at a 24% tax rate. These compare with the fund's implied donations of $5.1M in 2023 and $30.0M in 2024 from Healthwell filings.

Healthwell's blepharitis grants averaged $684 per recipient in 2023 and $680 in 2024 (Form 990), against a 12-month average of $750 on its website. Culper argues only XDEMVY ($1,850 per course) fits those averages. Natacyn, the only other high-priced listed drug, had $969,715 of Medicare Part D spending across 788 beneficiaries in 2024.

A Carepoint pharmacy representative estimated that 50% of XDEMVY Medicare patients use Healthwell grants. Applied to 57,626 Part D XDEMVY beneficiaries in 2024, that gives 28,813 patients, or 91% of the fund's 31,668 recipients.

The 2024 10-K named 'patient assistance donations' as a component of SG&A, while product revenue is recorded net of discounts. The 2025 10-K replaced the wording with 'patient support functions', grouped with IT, legal, professional and other expenses. Culper estimates that line grew from 11% to 29% of SG&A (2023 to Q1 2026).

Culper says 2026 profit estimates are too high. Consensus 2026 EBIT fell from +$84M (year-end 2024 view, on $503M revenue) to -$30M on about $696M revenue. The company guides to $670-700M net product sales and $545-565M SG&A. Q1 2026 SG&A was $136M, up from $131M the prior quarter, and 94% of revenue. Street models SG&A flat in dollars, which implies about 70% of revenue by year-end. Culper estimates 2026 EBIT of -$130M if SG&A holds at 94% of revenue.

BlinkRx has grown from 13% of revenue (2023) to 63% (2025). BlinkRx and Carepoint together were 79% in Q1 2026. Physicians told Culper that Tarsus reps direct prescriptions to BlinkRx, which routes Medicare patients to Healthwell. Culper argues this raises AKS concerns about indirect influence over the charity and patient choice of pharmacy.

Culper alleges BlinkRx pushes unneeded XDEMVY refills, which pulls forward reported growth and could raise False Claims Act medical necessity issues if billed to Medicare. One high-prescribing physician said 30-40% of their patients receive extra refills. Culper's own telehealth test produced an XDEMVY prescription with a one-year refill despite submitted photos of healthy eyelids.

Culper challenges the company's TAM of 25 million US demodex blepharitis patients, which comes from the Titan study (58% of eye care patients with collarettes, applied to 45 million annual patient visits). Culper says collarettes also occur in healthy patients. Its survey of 30 XDEMVY prescribers found 18% of patients (2,110 of 11,980) have DB and 12% have moderate to severe DB. Tarsus itself says only 1.5 million US patients have ever been diagnosed.

Tarsus has treated over 600,000 patients, about 40% of the 1.5 million diagnosed. The re-treatment rate is about 20%. Culper models XDEMVY revenue of $624M (2026), $759M (2027), $780M (2028), $751M (2029) and $655M (2030), against consensus of $696M, $905M, $1,086M, $1,263M and $1,455M. Revenue peaks below $800M in 2028 even if cumulative patients reach 3 million. The company's $2B+ claim implies over 1.7 million bottles a year.
In Q1 2026, XDEMVY revenue fell sequentially for the first time since launch, from $152M to $145M. Management cited deductible resets and temporarily reduced new patient visits.

Elanco sold its XDEMVY royalty stream to Blackstone for $295M in May 2025. At mid-to-high single-digit royalty rates, Culper estimates Blackstone underwrote peak revenue of $712M to $1,284M, against the company's $2B claim. Culper cites DoJ precedents: Actelion ($360M, Dec 2018), Jazz/Lundbeck/Alexion ($123M, Apr 2019), Incyte ($12.6M, May 2021) and Teva ($425M, Oct 2024). Insiders sold $17M of stock in the past year.

market_movers.rationale: Culper is short TARS on alleged Anti-Kickback Statute exposure from copay support through the Healthwell fund, an overstated TAM and 2026 profit estimates it says are too high. It expects revenue to peak below $800M at best. Culper issues fair values rather than price targets, and none is stated here.

earnings_insights: TARS Q1 2026 (reported): SG&A $136.4M vs $85.0M a year earlier (+61%). The company attributed $21.2M of the increase to patient support functions, IT, legal and professional expenses. XDEMVY revenue was $145M, down from $152M in Q4 2025. SG&A was 94% of revenue vs 86% in the prior quarter.
TARS 2026 company guidance (per CFO on Q4 2025 call): net product sales $670-700M, SG&A $545-565M, R&D $115-135M, gross margin about 93%. Culper cites a revenue midpoint of $685M.

TARS consensus (Bloomberg, per Culper): 2026 revenue $696M, 2026 EBIT -$30M. Street EBIT estimates are $163M for 2027 and $325M for 2028. At year-end 2024 the Street expected 2026 revenue of $503M and EBIT of $84M.

Culper estimate (not consensus): 2026 EBIT of -$130M if SG&A stays at 94% of revenue. Culper's XDEMVY revenue estimates are $624M (2026), $759M (2027) and $780M (2028), 10%, 16% and 28% below consensus.

TARS gross product sales were $328.7M in 2024 and $819.0M in 2025, against net sales of $180.1M and $451.4M, consistent with a gross-to-net discount of about 45%. Elanco received about $9M of royalty revenue in Q1 2026, an estimated 6.2% royalty rate.

trade_ideas.rationale: Culper says Tarsus's copay foundation practices expose it to a DoJ Anti-Kickback and False Claims Act action, XDEMVY revenue peaks below $800M, and 2026 profit estimates are too high.
trade_ideas.risk: The report does not state a specific risk to the short. It notes Tarsus may say its giving is set by factors other than XDEMVY sales.

risk_factors: Regulatory: a DoJ Anti-Kickback Statute or False Claims Act action could bring treble damages and exclusion from Medicare Part D. Culper calls this potentially devastating for a single-drug company.
Revenue risk: XDEMVY is a one-time six-week course with a roughly 20% re-treatment rate, and the pool of diagnosed patients is shrinking.
Q1 2026 XDEMVY revenue fell sequentially for the first time, and a former employee expects revenue to peak in late 2026 on payor pushback.
Customer concentration: BlinkRx was 63% of 2025 revenue, and BlinkRx plus Carepoint were 79% in Q1 2026.
Profitability risk: patient support spending scales with XDEMVY volume, and Street SG&A is modeled flat against guidance of $545-565M.
vol_and_positioning: Insiders sold $17M of TARS stock over the past year. No options, vol or short interest data is given.

theme_stances.evidence: Healthwell’s blepharitis fund appears to be effectively supported by a single manufacturer

theme_stances.key_argument: The 25 million patient TAM equates collarettes with disease, and the company's own data shows only 1.5 million diagnosed patients.
